title: Arvell Shaw's high playing; first recording Play, Fiddle, Play
summary: Crouch compares Arvell Shaw; Stewart says he first recorded Play, Fiddle, Play around 1943 with Garner, for Commodore or another label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Do you think that that -- I remember we were talking a little earlier today about that Arvell Shaw of pizzicato anyway --
-- plays or was playing in 1947 in the
recording he did with Louie Armstrong called Satchmo at Symphony Hall, which was done in Boston, wherein he plays -- he doesn't play that high.
But he was playing the bass then in the register that people began to play the bass after about 1960.

And although Mingus had played -- Mingus also played some pretty high things on bass, but pizzicato anyway. But it could be possible that -- did you ever talk with Arvell Shaw in the forties? Did you meet him then?
Do you recall when you met him?
Oh. When did you first record "Play, Fiddle, Play?"
I played it with -- as far back as when Erroll Garner was with me.
Sure. A little before then, even.
I had played it before I even met Erroll Garner. But what I was trying to say is I recorded
"Play, Fiddle, Play" when Erroll Garner was with me.
Do you know whether that recording is in circulation at this point or is it out of print?
I would doubt it very much.
Do you remember for whom you recorded it?
I recorded it for a label, was called at that time -- it was either Commodore or Okech.
